note: Rejudged 2026-10-31 by an auditor who authored neither the test nor its producer, after a third carrier was tagged. RFC 1195 Section 3.2: "In this case (assuming the entry is not superceded by a manually configured entry), then only one such entry shall be included in the level 2 LSP. The metric value(s) announced in level 2 LSPs correspond to the minimum of the metric value(s) that would be calculated for each of the level 1 LSP entries." The same section says directly reachable addresses "are treated exactly the same as addresses received in level 1 LSPs". New positive internal/plugins/isis/rfc1195_level2_reach_test.go::TestRFC1195Level2OneEntryPerPrefix runs the started engine, stores connected 172.30.0.0/24 at 10 and 192.0.2.0/24 at 50, applies a level 1 leak of both at 20, then decodes the stored level 2 LSP and requires exactly [10] and exactly [20] TLV 135 metrics: a duplicate or a non-minimum metric fails, and each case makes a different side win. Producer lsdb_wiring.go::level2Reachability, called for level 2 from the LSP state build; an observed red is recorded under a hand-written break that keeps every direct entry ([50 20] for 192.0.2.0/24). Earlier judgment of the other two carriers stands. Forbidden: more than one L2 entry for a prefix several L1 routers announce, or an L2 metric above the minimum. metricLeak fails unless exactly one L2 entry for the prefix is originated; TestRFC1195SpecificLeakCollapsesDuplicatePrefix (two routers, 20 and 9) and TestRFC1195SpecificLeakKeepsOnlyMinimum (three routers, 20, 12 and 9, cheapest not first in system-id order) each require metric 9. Distinct inputs, so no longer one assertion with two tags; a first-seen or last-seen leak producer fails the three-router case. No refusal path exists for an originator. Negative carries an observed-red record on leakInto; the positive has none but reads red on the same breaks.
